question: Can label-free geometric, spectral, invariance, and music-specific equivariance measurements identify which hidden layer of a frozen music foundation model will transfer best to a downstream music-information-retrieval task?

key_findings.claim: The best transferable layer is usually not the final layer, but its location depends jointly on pretraining paradigm and musical task family.
key_findings.evidence: Across the studied masked encoders, average performance peaks occur earliest for tonal tasks at about 30% depth, around 53% for semantic tasks, and around 64% for rhythm. Autoregressive models place most non-tonal optima in an intermediate band that tightens with scale while tonal optima shift deep; contrastive encoders place most non-tonal optima near the output but tonal optima earlier.

key_findings.claim: Intrinsic dimension is the most consistent standard proxy for non-tonal within-model layer quality, while temporal curvature supplies a complementary negative signal, especially for rhythm.
key_findings.evidence: Across non-tonal task families, intrinsic dimension has mean within-model Spearman correlation 0.76 and a consistent sign across masked, autoregressive, and contrastive paradigms. Curvature correlates negatively with beat/downbeat transfer in every masked model (-0.69/-0.76 on average) and autoregressive model (-0.68/-0.67). In larger autoregressive models, intrinsic-dimension correlations range from +0.65 to +0.97.

key_findings.claim: Generic geometry and invariance metrics fail on tonal tasks, whereas the proposed pitch-transposition-equivariance score tracks key, pitch, and chord layer quality much more consistently.
key_findings.evidence: Standard metrics have weak or sign-inconsistent tonal correlations. PTE has mean within-model correlation 0.80 overall, including 0.87 for pitch, 0.83 for key, and 0.59/0.63 for chord root/triads. Across models at their best layers, PTE correlations remain 1.00 for pitch, 0.75 for key, and 0.80 for chord.

key_findings.claim: Raw intrinsic metric values do not generally rank different model architectures, even when they rank layers within one model.
key_findings.evidence: Across models, effective rank correlates 0.82 with hidden dimension but only 0.02 with best-layer downstream quality. Within masked encoders, effective rank and intrinsic dimension correlate 0.70 with sequence-level transfer, but that association reverses for autoregressive models to -0.47. The paper therefore treats most metrics as within-model selectors rather than universal model scores.

anchors.section: 3.1 / Metrics do not yield reliable cross-model rankings

key_findings.claim: A top-three proxy shortlist recovers near-oracle layer performance with far fewer supervised probes, although the metric-to-task mapping is selected retrospectively from the same study.
key_findings.evidence: Training a probe only on the top proxy-ranked layer leaves a mean 1.0 percentage-point gap to the best single layer. Evaluating the top three lowers the gap to 0.4 points and matches or exceeds the oracle in 58% of model–task pairs, using about 4–16 times fewer supervised probe runs than exhaustive layer scanning.

key_findings.claim: Averaging only three proxy-ranked layers outperforms both indiscriminate fusion and the tested trainable fusion methods on average, especially with little labeled data.
key_findings.evidence: Top-three proxy-guided averaging has a mean oracle gap of 0.3 points and matches or exceeds the best single layer in 41% of pairs, versus gaps of 2.0 for all-layer averaging, 1.8 for learned weighted sum, 2.9 for HConv, and 2.7 for attentive fusion. For tasks with fewer than 1,000 training clips, every trainable baseline has a gap of at least 5.6 points; on 442-example GTZAN genre, every trainable fusion is at least 10 points below the oracle on average.

key_findings.claim: Layer-restricted fusion is not universally best: beat and chord recognition benefit from learned multi-layer aggregation, indicating genuinely distributed cues.
key_findings.evidence: HConv improves over the best single layer by 2.7–4.4 points on average for beat tracking and chord recognition, and attentive fusion improves by 1.7–3.3 points, with individual gains up to roughly 10 points. These are the only task groups where trainable fusion consistently exceeds the single-layer oracle.

method.core_idea: Measure each hidden layer of diverse frozen music models without downstream labels, correlate those intrinsic profiles with controlled downstream probe profiles, and use task-family-specific intrinsic metrics to shortlist or fuse layers.
method.mechanism: The study extracts every layer from 12 models covering masked, autoregressive, and contrastive pretraining on 10,000 fifteen-second MTG-Jamendo clips. Sequence representations are mean-pooled for encoders and taken from the final causal token for autoregressive decoders. Metrics include TwoNN intrinsic dimension, effective rank, anisotropy, temporal curvature, LiDAR, and InfoNCE under controlled augmentations. PTE trains the same small probe on an original clip and its 11 pitch-shifted versions, then scores whether their 12-bin key-signature profiles rotate by the expected circle-of-fifths phase. Each layer is separately evaluated with a fixed shallow probe across 15 downstream tasks. Within-model Spearman correlations choose a proxy per task family; the top one or three layers are then probed or fused and compared with fixed-depth, all-layer, weighted-sum, hierarchical-convolution, and attentive-fusion baselines.
assumptions: The fixed shallow downstream probe makes layer scores comparable and captures practically relevant transfer utility.
Ten thousand MTG-Jamendo clips adequately estimate intrinsic geometry for all twelve architectures.
Mean pooling is appropriate for encoder states and the final token adequately summarizes each autoregressive audio sequence.
Within-model rank correlation across depth reflects useful proxy alignment rather than a shared monotonic depth trend.
Task-family-specific metric choices learned in this benchmark transfer to new datasets, models, and deployments in the same family.
The selected augmentations preserve the relevant label except where pitch shifts are excluded for tonal tasks and time stretching for rhythm tasks.
PTE's learned self-supervised readout measures accessible transposition structure rather than probe capacity or artifacts of the pitch shifter.

techniques.role: Extracts and evaluates every hidden depth under one probe protocol rather than assuming the final layer is best.
Uses local neighbor-distance ratios to estimate how many degrees of freedom each layer's music manifold occupies.
Measures angles between successive frame-displacement vectors to detect layers whose audio trajectories become straighter.
Characterizes how evenly layer variance spreads across singular directions and how strongly one direction dominates.
Whitened between-clip versus within-augmentation scatter estimates how many stable clip-discriminative directions a layer provides.
Tests whether a shared layer readout rotates its tonal signature by the known semitone shift on the circle of fifths.
Ranks layers with a preselected intrinsic metric and spends supervised probe budget only on the top one or three.
Averages or concatenates only proxy-selected layers to reduce noise and estimation burden relative to all-layer fusion.
Uses partial Spearman checks to detect metric–performance associations that weaken or reverse after controlling for depth.

limitations: Author-stated: all reported metric–transfer relationships are correlational and do not show that manipulating intrinsic dimension, curvature, rank, invariance, or PTE will improve a representation.
Author-stated: objective, supervision, data, architecture, and scale co-vary across the available pretrained models, preventing causal attribution of the observed depth profiles.
Author-stated: no single metric works across all MIR tasks; useful proxies remain task- and paradigm-dependent.

Reviewer-identified: the task-family proxy is chosen retrospectively as the best-aligned metric in this same benchmark. Calling deployment label-free is locally true after selection, but the selection rule itself consumed downstream labels and needs prospective validation on unseen datasets and models.

Reviewer-identified: PTE is not a training-free scalar geometry statistic; it trains a layer-specific probe for up to 200 epochs using known transformation labels, so its compute and inductive supervision should be compared explicitly with a few ordinary downstream probes.

Reviewer-identified: correlations over adjacent layers violate independence and can be inflated by shared smooth depth trends; the paper notes partial-depth reversals but does not make depth-controlled results the primary selection criterion.
Reviewer-identified: one pooling convention per architecture family, a single fixed shallow probe class, and dataset-specific confounds can change which information appears accessible.

Reviewer-identified: the study reports broad average gaps but limited seed-level uncertainty for representation extraction, probe optimization, and selected-layer rankings; small differences such as 0.3 versus 0.4 points may not be operationally stable.

Reviewer-identified: Western 12-tone equal-tempered pitch shifts define PTE, so the proposed tonal proxy does not directly cover microtonal, non-Western, tuning-sensitive, or expressive intonation tasks.
failure_modes: A proxy learned on one benchmark chooses the wrong layer when a new dataset changes genre, production style, annotation policy, or task granularity.
Intrinsic rank or dimension mainly tracks hidden width, corpus diversity, or architecture, producing invalid cross-model comparisons.
A pitch shifter leaves spectral artifacts that a PTE probe can exploit without representing musically meaningful transposition.
Mean pooling erases local rhythmic or tonal events, while final-token pooling overweights recency or causal context length.
All strong layers encode redundant information, so averaging dilutes a narrow decisive signal; conversely, selecting only three layers misses complementary distributed cues for beat or chord tasks.
Low-data supervised fusion overfits scalar layer weights or attention, explaining why extra flexibility can underperform a fixed proxy average.
Metric–performance correlation is driven by depth rather than the claimed geometric mechanism and disappears on a different-depth model.
PTE cannot select a useful layer for tonal systems outside 12-TET or for tasks where invariance rather than equivariance to transposition is desired.
reusable_insights: Treat layer choice as a model-selection problem; the final hidden state is a baseline, not a default truth.
Use within-model metric ranks rather than raw cross-architecture values unless width and scale confounding have been calibrated.
Design intrinsic diagnostics around a task's transformation law: generic geometry misses structure that a domain-specific equivariance test can expose.
A cheap shortlist followed by a few supervised probes is more robust than trusting one unsupervised score as an oracle.
Restrict fusion to candidate layers before learning or averaging; including every layer can add both noise and estimation variance.
Report exceptions where distributed information favors multi-layer fusion instead of averaging them away in a global result.
Prospectively freeze the metric-to-task mapping before evaluating a new model or dataset to distinguish real zero-label selection from retrospective analysis.
open_questions: Do proxy mappings learned here select near-oracle layers prospectively on unseen music models, corpora, and task datasets?
Can controlled pretraining interventions change intrinsic dimension, curvature, or equivariance and establish a causal effect on transfer?
Can a single learned meta-proxy combine geometry and domain transformations without downstream labels for each new task family?
How much compute does PTE consume relative to top-three ordinary probes, and can a closed-form equivariance metric remove the trained readout?
Which layers transfer best under nonlinear, sequence-to-sequence, generative, retrieval, and few-shot adaptation rather than a fixed shallow probe?
Can uncertainty-aware shortlisting recognize flat profiles and avoid overclaiming a unique best layer?
What equivariance diagnostics cover rhythm scaling, timbre transformations, spatial audio, microtonality, and non-Western tonal systems?
Why do beat and chord tasks benefit from trainable fusion while most tagging and semantic tasks favor restricted averaging?

competitive_landscape.title: Layer-wise Investigation of Large-Scale Self-Supervised Music Representation Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhou et al. already map task information and single-layer performance through MusicFM and MuQ. The new paper broadens from two masked models to 12 masked, autoregressive, and contrastive systems, adds label-free geometric/transformation metrics, introduces PTE, and evaluates proxy-guided selection and fusion.

competitive_landscape.title: Layer by Layer: Uncovering Hidden Representations in Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Layer by Layer uses information-theoretic, geometric, and invariance measures to explain why intermediate language-model representations transfer well across 32 text tasks. The music study transports that framework across audio pretraining paradigms and shows generic metrics fail for tonality, motivating a music-specific transposition-equivariance diagnostic.

competitive_landscape.title: RankMe: Assessing the downstream performance of pretrained self-supervised representations by their rank
competitive_landscape.difference: RankMe proposes effective rank as a label-free representation-quality and hyperparameter-selection signal for joint-embedding SSL. The music study finds effective rank useful only in some within-model regimes, strongly confounded by hidden size across models, and weaker than intrinsic dimension or PTE for many tasks.

competitive_landscape.title: LiDAR: Sensing Linear Probing Performance in Joint Embedding SSL Architectures
competitive_landscape.difference: LiDAR improves rank-based SSL assessment by whitening augmentation variation and measuring surrogate-class discriminability. The music study applies it layerwise, finds it correlated with ID/curvature in masked encoders but architecture-dependent in autoregressive models, and combines it with other task-family proxies rather than treating it as universal.

competitive_landscape.title: Uncovering the Latent Potential of Deep Intermediate Representations
competitive_landscape.difference: LOES constructs task-discriminative layer subspaces under orthogonality/isotropy constraints and introduces GeoReg to preserve geometry during fine-tuning across modalities, using task supervision for its strongest selection mode. The music paper emphasizes no-downstream-label diagnostics and task-family proxy shortlists, with deeper music-specific coverage but no causal regularizer.

competitive_landscape.title: Do Music Generation Models Encode Music Theory?
competitive_landscape.difference: SynTheory probes explicit tempo, pitch, interval, scale, chord, and progression concepts across Jukebox and MusicGen layers using synthetic labels. The new study asks whether unlabeled intrinsic properties predict real downstream transfer and introduces PTE as a transformation-based proxy rather than directly decoding named theory concepts.

competitive_landscape.title: Codified audio language modeling learns useful representations for music information retrieval
competitive_landscape.difference: This work establishes that intermediate Jukebox features transfer strongly to four MIR tasks and can beat tagging-pretrained representations. The new paper generalizes layer analysis far beyond Jukebox, asks why certain layers work through intrinsic measurements, and turns those measurements into a selection policy.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: this is the first systematic intrinsic-property analysis of music foundation models across layers and masked, autoregressive, and contrastive paradigms; PTE supplies the missing tonal signal; and intrinsic proxies enable near-oracle label-free layer selection and restricted fusion. Reviewer inference after primary-work comparison: intermediate-layer transfer, effective-rank/LiDAR quality proxies, general geometric layer analysis, and music-model probing are all established separately. The credible novelty is their unusually broad 12-model/15-task music synthesis, the empirical demonstration that generic metrics fail specifically on tonality, the circle-of-fifths PTE diagnostic, and a practical top-three proxy shortlist. The 'label-free' operational claim is conditional because the best proxy per task family is chosen retrospectively using labeled downstream correlations; prospective frozen-mapping validation remains necessary.
reviewer_notes: The complete 11-page paper was checked, including model/metric definitions, all downstream tasks, correlation qualifications, selection/fusion table, conclusions, and bibliography. Primary records were reviewed for the closest music-layer study, RankMe, LiDAR, Layer by Layer, LOES, SynTheory, and JukeMIR. Numerical values come from Sections 3.1–3.2 and Table 2; PTE is described as self-supervised rather than strictly training-free because it fits a transformation-supervised readout at every layer.
